The evidence yields a composite answer because the query "when did the first settlers arrive" lacks a specific scope. The documents collectively offer several correct dates for different groups and definitions, which can be combined without contradiction.

The question "when did the first settlers arrive" is ambiguous, as it could refer to the first humans, the first Europeans, or the first permanent settlers of a specific nation. The retrieved documents provide complementary answers for different scopes [d1, d2, d5, d6, d7]. The first human settlers arrived between 19,000 and 26,000 years ago [d5]. The first permanent European settlement in the Americas was Santo Domingo in 1496 [d1, d6]. The first permanent English settlement was Jamestown, with colonists arriving in April 1607 and selecting the site on May 13, 1607 [d2, d4, d8, d9]. For the colony of Georgia, the first settlers arrived in 1733 [d3, d7].
